topics.title: Stem-and-leaf plots and back-to-back stem-and-leaf plots

questions.stem: The monthly car sales for 16 dealerships are shown. Make an ordered stem-and-leaf plot.
questions.answer: Sample answer: use the ordered stem-and-leaf plot shown. Key: 3 | 7 = 37 cars. The leaves are ordered within each stem.
questions.hint: Sort the values first, then use the tens digits as stems and list the units digits as ordered leaves.

keyPoints.note: There should be one leaf for every data value.
Keep each row of leaves in ascending order.

steps.explain: Order all 16 sales values from least to greatest before separating tens and units.
Use each tens digit as a stem and order the units digits as leaves.
Check that each leaf represents one original value and that there are 16 leaves.

questions.stem: The marks of 10 students on an examination are shown in the stem-and-leaf plot below (key: $5|7 = 57$). What is the mean examination mark for these students?

steps.explain: Read off every individual mark from the stem-and-leaf plot (stem = tens digit, leaf = units digit), in order.
Add all ten marks together to find the total.
The mean is the sum divided by the number of data values ($n=10$).

questions.stem: Find the median of the data presented in the dot plot below.

steps.explain: Find the total number of data points by adding up every score's frequency (dot count).
List every value in ascending order using the given frequencies: one $1$, three $2$s, two $3$s, one $4$, one $6$.
Since $n=8$ is even, the median is the average of the $\frac{n}{2}$th and $\left(\frac{n}{2}+1\right)$th values — i.e. the 4th and 5th values in the ordered list.
Average these two middle values to find the median.

questions.stem: Using the 16 dealership sales data, what is the median number of cars sold?
questions.hint: Read the data in order and average the two middle values because there are 16 values.

keyPoints.note: With an even number of data values, average the two central values.
First order the data, then locate positions 8 and 9.

steps.explain: There are 16 observations, so the median is the mean of positions 8 and 9.
The 8th and 9th ordered values are 47 and 48.

questions.stem: For the data set 29, 24, 30, 11, 32, 29, 24, 26, 25, 28, 29, find the median.
questions.hint: Order the 11 values; with an odd count, the median is the 6th value.

keyPoints.note: Sort all observations before finding the middle value.

steps.explain: Order the values from least to greatest.
There are 11 values, so select position 6.

questions.stem: For the data set 29, 24, 30, 11, 32, 29, 24, 26, 25, 28, 29, find the mean.
questions.hint: Add the values, then divide by the number of values.

keyPoints.note: The mean uses every data value: sum ÷ count.

steps.explain: To 2 decimal places, the mean is 26.09.
